messages:
elaine: Quick follow-up from the RFC — I want to capture the decisions around a compatibility shim between our legacy rule DSL and the proposed rule-compiler IR. Short thread to sync on tradeoffs and rollout plan.

mike: TL;DR: my proposal is a thin translation shim that compiles legacy rules to a compact IR on first use and caches the compiled bytecode keyed by a policy fingerprint. That lets us ship the new runtime without forcing all tenants to immediately rewrite rules. :thumbsup:

mike: Benefits: zero-downtime migration, incremental rollout, and we avoid keeping two evaluators in hot-path. Costs: added compile-on-warm latency and cache management.

jamie: Concern: compile-on-warm in the hot path can spike p99. We should precompile at deploy time for service-level policies and only JIT tenant-inline policies.

suresh: Agreed. Suggestion: two modes — precompile (CI step) + cached bytecode, and safe-JIT for ad-hoc tenant rules with a compilation budget throttle. Instrumentation: policy.compile.latency, policy.compile.failures, policy.eval.hotpath-ms.

mike: Implementation sketch:
```
# legacy rule
rule {
  id: "eu_bias"
  expr: "region == 'eu' ? -10 : 0"
}
# compiler output: fingerprinted bytecode
fingerprint: sha256:abc123
bytecode: <binary>
```
Cache key: tenant_id + rule_id + version + compile_fingerprint. Evict LRU, but protect recently compiled that are hot.

elaine: For rollout: 1) add feature flag that enables IR path per service, 2) precompile global rules at build time, 3) enable JIT with a tiny budget (e.g. 20 compiles/5min) for tenants, 4) add fallback to legacy evaluator on compile error.

jamie: Ops note: we need a backpressure plan. If compilation saturates CPUs during traffic spikes we should be able to reject compilation requests and mark rule as "degraded" in the decision trace. Also add a metric policy.compile.rejected.

suresh: Compatibility edge cases: macros, external function hooks, and tenant-side templates. We should whitelist/export a small set of runtime-safe builtins during translation. Anything else falls back to legacy engine.

mike: On policy size/complexity: propose a hard limit on AST nodes for auto-compiled rules; larger rules flagged for manual migration. Also add an offline lint that suggests cost-reducing transforms (e.g., normalize nested ORs into table lookups).

elaine: Testing: unit compiler tests, golden bytecode diffs, end-to-end perf tests that simulate 95/99/999 tails under mixed precompiled+JIT workload. We'll track: policy.eval.latency.{p50,p95,p99}, policy.compile.duration, policy.compile.rate.

jamie: Rollout canaries: start with internal tenants -> low-traffic customers -> all. Use the feature flag targeting system and an automatic rollback if p99 inference latency increases > 10% for 10m.

mike: Open questions:
- How do we expose compile failures to tenants without leaking infra details? (error classes not stack traces)
- Should compiled bytecode be persisted across restarts (yes?) and how to secure it? (encrypt at rest + sign)

suresh: My take: persist compiled bytecode in the node-local store with optional remote cache (S3-like) for warm start. All persisted artifacts must be signed by the compiler service key. Tenants see friendly error codes: COMPILE_FAIL, FALLBACK_ACTIVE.

elaine: Action items:
- @mike: prototype translation + fingerprinted cache (P0) — due EOW
- @jamie: add compile throttling circuit and perf tests (P0)
- @suresh: flesh out storage encryption/signing and error mapping (P1)
- @infra-bot: start canary once prototype lands — small internal cohort first

mike: +1. I'll open a PR with a minimal compiler and AB test hooks. Expect some follow-up threads for telemetry dashboards.

elaine: Awesome. If no objections I'll lock this as the follow-up plan and add the checklist to the RFC doc. :white_check_mark:
